title: Fresh
brief: An open-source terminal IDE with zero configuration that brings VS Code-style UX — familiar keybindings, full mouse support, command palette — to the shell. It packs IDE-level features including LSP, multi-cursor editing, magit-style git review with per-hunk staging, TypeScript plugins, multi-GB file handling, and SSH remote editing, plus an orchestrator that runs coding agents (claude, codex, opencode, aider) across worktrees.
details: Fresh (getfresh.dev) — "the terminal IDE, refined": a Rust-built terminal IDE that behaves like a modern GUI editor — Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+C copies, full mouse support, menus, command palette, multi-cursor, no modes to learn (vim mode optional). The standout is the Orchestrator: every task gets its own git worktree with its own tabs, terminals, and agent — hop between tasks with an arrow key while the rest keep working. Each workspace can run any terminal coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or your own command), agents that can resume pick up after restarts, and an agent-facing CLI (`fresh --cmd`, `fresh --skill`) lets agents organize workspaces, start sessions, and drive the editor. Also: hunk-level git review dock, side-by-side diffs, multi-GB files without blocking, SSH/Kubernetes/dev-container remotes, multi-LSP per language, detachable daemon with hot exit, TypeScript plugins in a sandbox, and one static binary installable via curl/Homebrew/winget/AUR/npm. Open source (GPL-3.0). Enthusiastic reception from the terminal-editor crowd.
